'''Ian Michael Macdonald''' (born 7 March 1949) is a former [[Australia]]n politician and currently undergoing court proceedings and was a member of the [[New South Wales Legislative Council]] from 1988 to 2010 representing the [[Australian Labor Party (New South Wales Branch)|Labor Party]]. Between 2003 and 2010, Macdonald held a range of ministerial responsibilities in the [[Bob Carr|Carr]], [[Morris Iemma|Iemma]], [[Nathan Rees|Rees]], and [[Kristina Keneally|Keneally]] ministries.<ref name=nsw>{{Cite NSW Parliament |id=2216 |name=Mr Ian Michael Macdonald (1949- ) |former=Yes |access-date=22 June 2020}}</ref> Macdonald, who joined the Labor Party in 1972, had his membership of the party terminated in 2013 for bringing the party into disrepute.<ref name=expell>{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-06-06/obeid-and-macdonald-expelled-from-labor-party/4736322 |title=Eddie Obeid and Ian Macdonald expelled from Labor Party |author=Harvey, Eliza |date=6 June 2013 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |access-date=13 November 2013 }}</ref>

After the [[Independent Commission Against Corruption (New South Wales)|Independent Commission Against Corruption]] found that he acted in a corrupt manner,<ref name="ICAC4"/> Macdonald was [[criminal charge|charged]] with the offence of misconduct in public office for corruptly issuing lucrative mining licences at Doyles Creek in the Hunter Valley,<ref name=SMHprosecution/><ref name=ABCprosecution/> found guilty by a [[Supreme Court of New South Wales|Supreme Court]] jury in March 2017,<ref name="ABC guilty"/> and sentenced in June 2017 for a period of ten years, with a minimum custodial period of seven years.<ref name="SMH sentence1">{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/from-pinot-to-porridge-ian-macdonald-to-spend-seven-years-behind-bars-20170602-gwjfem.html |title=From pinot to porridge, Ian Macdonald to spend seven years behind bars |date=3 June 2017 |access-date=3 June 2017 |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |author=McClymont, Kate }}</ref><ref name="ABC sentence1">{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-06-02/macdonald-and-maitland-jailed-over-mining-licence-deal/8580914 |title=Ian Macdonald jailed for 10 years for misconduct in public office, John Maitland also imprisoned |date=2 June 2017 |access-date=3 June 2017 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |author1=Chettle, Nicole |author2=Stuart, Riley }}</ref><ref name="DT sentence1">{{cite news |url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/news/nsw/former-labor-minister-ian-mcdonald-sentenced-to-ten-years-for-misconduct-in-public-office/news-story/68ce44fa8fd9301326c98e246a4b568d |title=Former Labor minister Ian Macdonald sentenced to 10 years for misconduct in public office |date=2 June 2017 |access-date=2 June 2017 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|The Telegraph]] |location=Australia |author=Parthridge, Emma }}</ref> Macdonald [[appeal]]ed against the verdict and, on 25 February 2019, his conviction was [[Motion to quash|quashed]] by the [[New South Wales Court of Criminal Appeal|NSW Court of Criminal Appeal]] who ordered a retrial. He was granted bail and released from custody on the same day.<ref name="ABC quash1">{{cite news |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-02-25/ian-macdonald-wins-appeal-against-misconduct-conviction/10845314 |title=Ian Macdonald wins appeal against misconduct conviction, walks free from prison |date=25 February 2019 |access-date=25 February 2019 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |author1=Wells, Jamelle }}</ref><ref name="Herald quash">{{cite news |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/5921703/ian-macdonald-john-maitland-misconduct-convictions-quashed/ |author=Thompson, Angus |title=Ian Macdonald, John Maitland misconduct convictions quashed |work=[[The Newcastle Herald|The Herald]] |location=Newcastle |date=25 February 2019 |access-date=25 February 2019 }}</ref><ref name="SMH quash">{{cite news |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/nsw/former-nsw-labor-minister-ian-macdonald-and-union-friend-john-maitland-s-convictions-thrown-out-20190225-p51002.html |author=Thompson, Angus |title=Ex-NSW Labor minister Ian Macdonald and union friend John Maitland's convictions thrown out |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=25 February 2019 |access-date=25 February 2019 }}</ref> In July 2021 Macdonald was found guilty of misconduct in public office on separate charges relating to the granting of a lucrative coal-exploration licence over Cherrydale Park, in the [[Bylong Valley]], owned by the family of [[Eddie Obeid]].<ref name="SMHverdict2021"/><ref name="ABCverdict2021"/><ref name="GAverdict2021"/>

==Early career and background==
Raised as one of five children by his mother in a single parent household,<ref name="maiden">{{cite web|title=Independent Commission Against Corruption Bill (No.2) – Second reading|work=[[Hansard]] – extract|publisher=[[Legislative Council of New South Wales]]|url=http://www.parliament.nsw.gov.au/Prod/Parlment/Members.nsf/d890a06557517cedca256e700008765e/75b5906290a3dd464a25672e0002e1d8/$FILE/First%20Speech.Macdonald.pdf|date=8 June 1988|access-date=21 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023233001/http://www.parliament.nsw.gov.au/Prod/Parlment/Members.nsf/d890a06557517cedca256e700008765e/75b5906290a3dd464a25672e0002e1d8/%24FILE/First%20Speech.Macdonald.pdf|archive-date=23 October 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Macdonald graduated from [[La Trobe University]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] [[Bachelor's degree#Honours Degrees and academic distinctions|(Honours)]] in history and worked for the Australian Council of Overseas Aid, and a range of Commonwealth and State government agencies before his election to parliament in 1988.<ref name=nsw/>

At the time of entering Parliament, he was a farmer near [[Carcoar, New South Wales|Carcoar]] in the [[Central West (New South Wales)|Central West]] of New South Wales.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.abc.net.au/rural/nsw/stories/s823796.htm|title=New Minister for Agriculture|work=[[ABC Rural#Radio|The Country Hour]]|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]|date=3 April 2003 |access-date=21 May 2011}}</ref>

==Political career==
Elected to the Legislative Council in 1988, Macdonald was appointed [[Minister for Primary Industries (New South Wales)|Minister for Agriculture and Fisheries]] in 2003 and then the Primary Industries portfolio and a range of other portfolios in the [[Iemma ministry (2005–2007)|first]] and [[Iemma ministry (2007–2008)|second Iemma]] and [[Rees ministry|Rees]] ministries including Natural Resources, Mineral Resources, State Development, and Energy. However, granted extraordinary powers by Labor State Conference on 17 November 2009, Rees sacked Macdonald (along with others) from the ministry because of Macdonald's efforts to destabilise Rees in his position.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/national/rees-crackdown-ministers-axed-from-nsw-cabinet-20091115-ig5u.html |title=Rees crackdown: ministers axed from NSW cabinet |date=15 November 2009 |access-date=15 November 2009 |work=The Sydney Morning Herald }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/449011/sacked-hornery-to-keep-fighting-for-wallsend-centre/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121203012458/http://www.theherald.com.au/news/local/news/general/sacked-hornery-to-keep-fighting-for-wallsend-centre/1679041.aspx |url-status=live |archive-date=3 December 2012 |work=[[Newcastle Herald]] |title=Hornery to Keep Fighting |author=Dinneen, Martin |date=17 November 2009 |access-date=20 November 2009 }}</ref>

Macdonald then played a large part in the sacking of Rees in favour of Keneally.{{citation needed|date=December 2011}} Macdonald was previously a member of the New South Wales [[Socialist Left (Australia)|Socialist Left]] faction, but was formally expelled in December 2009 for his role in Rees's downfall.{{citation needed|date=December 2011}} Keneally restored Macdonald to the ministry following her election as Premier, making him the [[Minister for Major Events (New South Wales)|Minister for Major Events]], Mineral and Forest Resources, State and Regional Development and Central Coast.

Macdonald was plagued by scandal surrounding a trip to Dubai made in 2008, which led him to resign from the ministry on 4 June 2010<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/keneally-loses-another-minister-20100604-xkd1.html |title=Keneally loses another minister |last=Hall |first=Louise |date=4 June 2010 |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=7 June 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100605194601/http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/keneally-loses-another-minister-20100604-xkd1.html |archive-date=5 June 2010 }}</ref> on the same day as the resignation of Minister [[Graham West]]. Macdonald's Dubai trip was investigated by the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) after a government report found he misused public funds.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/corruption-watchdog-to-investigate-macdonalds-expenses-20100610-xznx.html|title=Corruption watchdog to investigate Macdonald's expenses|date=10 June 2010|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=13 June 2010}}</ref>

On 7 June 2010 Macdonald resigned from parliament with immediate effect.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/expenses-errors-macdonald-quits-nsw-parliament-20100607-xq5m.html |title=Expenses errors: Macdonald quits NSW parliament |last=Nicholls |first=Sean |date=7 June 2010 |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=7 June 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100610205700/http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/expenses-errors-macdonald-quits-nsw-parliament-20100607-xq5m.html |archive-date=10 June 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/opinion/politics/the-party-was-over-long-before-macca-jumped-20100605-xlt1.html#ixzz1R1UirKUq |title=The party was over long before 'Macca' jumped |author=Mitchell, Alex |date=6 June 2010 |work=The Brisbane Times |publisher=Fairfax Media |access-date=3 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100608043933/http://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/opinion/politics/the-party-was-over-long-before-macca-jumped-20100605-xlt1.html |archive-date=8 June 2010 }}</ref> He was replaced by [[Luke Foley]], the assistant general secretary of the New South Wales Labor Party.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/stories/2010/06/09/2922892.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100612100711/http://www.abc.net.au/news/stories/2010/06/09/2922892.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 June 2010 |title=Labor announces Macdonald replacement |work=ABC News |location=Australia |date=10 June 2010 |access-date=14 June 2010}}</ref>

In July 2012 Macdonald was suspended by the Australian Labor Party for "conduct contrary to the principles of the party".<ref>{{cite news|last=Nicholls|first=Sean|title=Labor axes trio in bid to rebuild|url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/labor-axes-trio-in-bid-to-rebuild-20120712-21yyw.html|access-date=13 July 2012|newspaper=smh.com.au|date=13 July 2012}}</ref> His membership was subsequently terminated in mid-2013 for bringing the party in disrepute.<ref name=expell/>

===ICAC inquiries into alleged corrupt behaviour===
In November 2011 the ICAC commenced an inquiry that heard allegations that Macdonald, while Minister, accepted sexual favours in return for introducing businessman to executives of state-owned energy companies. It was also alleged that property developer [[Ron Medich]] acted as a broker for Macdonald and was seeking to do business with government agencies where Macdonald had influence as a minister.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/tiffanie-and-the-minister-macdonald-accepted-sexual-services-arranged-by-medich-inquiry-hears-20111124-1nvsb.html |title=Tiffanie and the minister: Macdonald accepted sexual services arranged by Medich, inquiry hears |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |author1=Nicholls, Sean |author2=McClymont, Kate |date=24 November 2011 |access-date=24 November 2011}}</ref> Appearing before the commission to give evidence in relation to the allegations, Macdonald claimed that he was under the influence of alcohol and suffering the effects of depression at the time of the alleged incident.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/i-couldnt-see-properly-macdonalds-twobot-night-with-tiffanie-20111202-1oajx.html |title=I couldn't see properly; Macdonald's two bot night with Tiffanie |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=2 December 2011 |access-date=2 December 2011 }}</ref>

In November 2012, the ICAC began a series of investigative [[Hearing (law)|hearings]] relating to Macdonald and the property and mining interests of [[Eddie Obeid]], a former Labor minister and "[[Power broker (term)|power broker]]".<ref name="SMH-see you right">{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/cgi-bin/common/popupPrintArticle.pl?path=/articles/2003/02/24/1046063962405.html |last1=Totaro |first1=Paula |last2=Wainwright |first2=Robert |title=Dump the Left, and Eddie Obeid will see you right |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=25 February 2003 |access-date=7 March 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040526154755/http://www.smh.com.au/cgi-bin/common/popupPrintArticle.pl?path=%2Farticles%2F2003%2F02%2F24%2F1046063962405.html |archive-date=26 May 2004 |url-status=dead }}</ref> This inquiry concerned, among other issues, the circumstances surrounding a decision made in 2008 by Macdonald as the [[Minister for Primary Industries (New South Wales)|Minister for Primary Industries and Minister for Mineral Resources]], to open a mining area in the [[Bylong, New South Wales|Bylong Valley]] for coal exploration. These circumstances include whether Macdonald's decision was influenced by Obeid.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4182 |title=Public inquiry into circumstances surrounding decision to open Bylong Valley mining area for coal exploration |date=9 November 2012 |work=Operation Jasper |publisher=[[Independent Commission Against Corruption (New South Wales)|Independent Commission Against Corruption]] |access-date=15 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121115000414/http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4182 |archive-date=15 November 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The witnesses list for the inquiry included former [[Premier of New South Wales|NSW Premiers]] [[Morris Iemma]] and [[Nathan Rees]].<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/images/L-Witness_List_Jasper_PI_Week_of_12_November_2012.pdf |title=Witness list for the Operation Jasper Segment |date=9 November 2012 |work=Operations Indus/Jasper/Acacia Public Inquiry |publisher=Independent Commission Against Corruption |access-date=15 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924032518/http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/images/L-Witness_List_Jasper_PI_Week_of_12_November_2012.pdf |archive-date=24 September 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2012-11-13/iemma-gives-evidence-to-icac-hearing/4368798 |title=Iemma tells ICAC of relationship between Obeid, Macdonald |work=ABC News |location=Australia |author=Wells, Jamelle |date=13 November 2012 |access-date=15 November 2012 |format=transcript, video, audio }}</ref>

On 31 July 2013 the commission found that Macdonald engaged in corrupt conduct by exercising his ministerial influence to arrange a meeting between Ron Medich and [[Country Energy]] managing director Craig Murray on 15 July 2009, and, prior to the meeting, by soliciting the services of a woman as a reward for arranging the meeting.<ref name="ICAC1">{{cite press release |title=ICAC finds former minister Ian Macdonald corrupt over rewards for facilitating meeting with energy executive |date=31 July 2013 |publisher=[[Independent Commission Against Corruption (New South Wales)|Independent Commission Against Corruption]] |url=http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4385 |access-date=31 July 2013 |archive-date=29 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161129052148/http://icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4385/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The commission also found that Macdonald acted contrary to his public duty as a minister of the Crown by arranging for the creation of the Mount Penny tenement to benefit members of the Obeid family, and that he acted contrary to his public duty as a minister of the Crown by providing members of the Obeid family with confidential information that was to their benefit. Further, the commission found that Macdonald acted corruptly by deciding to reopen the expressions of interest process for mining exploration licences in order to favour Travers Duncan, and by providing him with confidential information.<ref name="ICAC2">{{cite press release |title=ICAC finds corrupt conduct over Mount Penny tenement |date=31 July 2013 |publisher=[[Independent Commission Against Corruption (New South Wales)|Independent Commission Against Corruption]] |url=http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4395 |access-date=31 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130805055047/http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4395 |archive-date=5 August 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The commission recommended that the above matters be referred to the [[Director of Public Prosecutions (New South Wales)|director of public prosecutions]] (DPP) with respect to prosecuting Macdonald.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/nation/politics/ian-macdonald-eddie-obeid-facing-charges-after-being-found-by-icac-to-have-acted-corruptly/news-story/9d218f59fa35014749763fe4c69eb777 |work=[[The Australian]] |date=31 July 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013 |title=Ian Macdonald, Eddie Obeid facing charges after being found by ICAC to have acted corruptly |author=Shanahan, Leo |archive-date=2013-08-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130801213036/http://www.theaustralian.com.au/national-affairs/state-politics/ian-macdonald-eddie-obeid-facing-charges-after-being-found-by-icac-to-have-acted-corruptly/story-e6frgczx-1226688614716 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |agency=AAP }}</ref><ref name="abc20130731">{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-07-31/icac-findings-released/4855128 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |date=31 July 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013 |title=ICAC recommends charges against former NSW Labor ministers Eddie Obeid and Ian Macdonald |author1=Wells, Jamelle |author2=Gerathy, Sarah }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/eddie-obeid-ian-macdonald-acted-corruptly-icac-finds-20130731-2qy67.html |title=Eddie Obeid, Ian Macdonald acted corruptly, ICAC finds |author1=Olding, Rachel |author2=Waters, Georgia |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=31 July 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013 }}</ref> On reviewing the evidence before the commission of the financial benefits accrued to the Obeid family, the ICAC provided relevant information to the [[New South Wales Crime Commission|NSW Crime Commission]] for such action as it deems appropriate, and the ICAC also disseminated relevant information to the [[Australian Taxation Office]] for appropriate action.<ref name="ICAC2"/> Macdonald vowed to launch a court challenge against the corruption findings made against him by the Independent Commission Against Corruption.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-07-31/ian-macdonald-vows-to-launch-court-challenge-to-corruption-find/4856594 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |date=31 July 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013 |title=Ian Macdonald vows to launch court challenge against corruption findings |author2=Oriti, Thomas |author1=Gerathy, Sarah }}</ref>

One month later, the ICAC made further findings that Macdonald engaged in corrupt conduct by acting contrary to his duty as a minister of the Crown in granting consent to Doyles Creek Mining Pty Ltd to apply for a coal [[Tenement (law)|exploration licence]] at Doyles Creek and by granting the exploration licence to the company, both grants being substantially for the purpose of benefiting John Maitland, a former official of the [[Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union]]. The commission found that, but for that purpose, Macdonald would not have made those grants.<ref name="ICAC4">{{cite press release |title=ICAC finds corrupt conduct in relation to Doyles Creek coal exploration licence |date=30 August 2013 |publisher=[[Independent Commission Against Corruption (New South Wales)|Independent Commission Against Corruption]] |url=http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4398 |access-date=6 January 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304044940/http://www.icac.nsw.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/article/4398 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/ian-macdonald-found-corrupt-by-icac-again-20130830-2surh.html |title=Ian Macdonald found corrupt by ICAC again |author1=Besser, Linton |author2=Nicholls, Sean |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=30 August 2013 |access-date=6 January 2014 }}</ref> In January 2014, the premier, [[Barry O'Farrell]], announced that the [[Liberal Party of Australia (New South Wales Division)|Liberal]]/[[National Party of Australia – NSW|National]] government would introduce legislation into Parliament to cancel the exploration licences for Doyles Creek, Mount Penny and Glendon Brook.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-01-20/nsw-government-to-cancel-licences-for-hunter-valley-mines-at-th/5209394 |title=NSW to cancel licences for Hunter Valley mines at centre of ICAC corruption findings |author=Kennedy, Jean |author2= and staff |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |date=21 January 2014 |access-date=22 January 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Nicholls, Sean |author2=Whitbourn, Michaela |title=NSW government cancels mining licences tainted by Eddie Obeid, Ian Macdonald corruption scandals |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/nsw-government-cancels-mining-licences-tainted-by-eddie-obeid-ian-macdonald-corruption-scandals-20140120-314iv.html#ixzz2r7zyDQyq |date=20 January 2014 |access-date=22 January 2014 |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] }}</ref> The commission also made findings of corrupt conduct by Obeid and his son, Moses Obeid, John Maitland, and others.<ref name="ICAC4"/><ref name="ICAC3">{{cite press release |title=ICAC finds corrupt conduct in relation to benefit to former minister |date=31 July 2013 |publisher=[[Independent Commission Against Corruption (New South In November 2014 the ICAC announced that Macdonald will be prosecuted by the DPP for the offence of misconduct in public office for corruptly issuing of lucrative mining licences at Doyles Creek in the Hunter Valley.<ref name=SMHprosecution>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/former-labor-minister-ian-macdonald-prosecuted-over-doyles-creek-mine-deal-20141120-11qbch.html|title=Former Labor minister Ian Macdonald prosecuted over Doyles Creek mine deal|author1=Nicholls, Sean|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|date=20 November 2014|access-date=21 November 2014}}</ref><ref name=ABCprosecution>{{cite news|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-11-20/ian-macdonald-eddie-obeid-to-be-prosecuted/5905540|work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]]|location=Australia|date=20 November 2014|access-date=21 November 2014|title=ICAC: Former NSW ministers Eddie Obeid and Ian Macdonald to be prosecuted after corruption findings}}</ref> Macdonald was also prosecuted "for two counts of being an accessory before the fact to misconduct in public office, in relation to aiding, abetting, counselling and procuring the commission of the two offences by Mr Macdonald"; and for giving false and misleading evidence to the ICAC.<ref name=SMHprosecution/>

In December 2015, the Supreme Court heard that Macdonald was unable to secure [[Legal aid#Australia|Legal Aid]] funding to pay for legal representation in his criminal trial. The Judge commented that a [[Dietrich v The Queen|''Dietrich'' application]] was a "potential collateral challenge to the trial date."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/disgraced-former-mp-ian-macdonald-fails-to-secure-funding-for-criminal-trial-20151204-glfi1b.html#ixzz4Ct5khY87 |title=Disgraced former MP Ian Macdonald fails to secure funding for criminal trial |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=4 December 2015 |access-date=29 June 2016 |author=Hall, Louisa }}</ref> It was estimated that Macdonald's defence legal costs would be between {{AUD}}250,000 and {{AUD}}1.5&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/legal-affairs/refusal-of-legal-aid-risks-stalling-trial-of-ian-macdonald/news-story/cc6fc9a7ca5d5628c84bca82a23edce6 |title=Refusal of legal aid risks stalling trial of Ian Macdonald |work=[[The Australian]] |date=27 January 2016 |access-date=29 June 2016 |url-access=subscription |author=Merritt, Chris }}</ref> In March 2017 a criminal trial before a Supreme Court jury found that Macdonald was guilty of misconduct in public office.<ref name="ABC guilty">{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-03-30/ian-macdonald-found-guilty-of-misconduct-in-public-office/8392458 |title=Ian Macdonald found guilty of misconduct in public office, John Maitland guilty as accessory |date=30 March 2017 |access-date=3 June 2017 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia }}</ref> Sentenced on 2 June, Macdonald is serving a ten-year sentence, of which seven years were without [[parole]].<ref name="SMH sentence1"/><ref name="ABC sentence1"/><ref name="DT sentence1"/> Immediately following his sentencing, Macdonald's lawyers advised that he would [[appeal]] against his conviction. The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal handed down its findings on 25 February 2019 and quashed Macdonald and Maitland's convictions, ordering a retrial. Both men were released from custody on the same day and granted bail. In handing down its findings the Court found that:<ref name="ABC quash1"/><ref name="Herald quash"/><ref name="SMH quash"/>
{{blockquote|.... [trial judge — Justice Christine Adamson] "misdirected" the jurors about the state of mind needed to be found guilty of wilful misconduct in public office. It follows, in our opinion, with the greatest respect to the trial judge, that the jury was not properly directed on the mental element of the offence.|[[New South Wales Court of Criminal Appeal]] judgement, February 2019.}}

Prior to his sentencing, the NSW Parliament passed legislation to remove parliamentary pensions from former politicians convicted of serious criminal offences.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/nsw/eddie-obeid-and-ian-macdonald-to-be-stripped-of-nsw-parliamentary-pensions-20170523-gwb409.html |title=Eddie Obeid and Ian Macdonald to be stripped of NSW parliamentary pensions |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=23 May 2017 |access-date=3 June 2017 |author=Nicholls, Sean }}</ref>

In late May 2017 Macdonald was also committed to stand trial on conspiracy charges with Obeid, and his son, Moses Obeid, relating to Macdonald's granting of a coal exploration licence involving the Mount Penny tenement;<ref name="SMH sentence1"/><ref name="ABC sentence1"/> due to commence in March 2019.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/oct/06/former-nsw-ministers-ian-macdonald-and-eddie-obeid-to-face-trial-in-2019 |title=Former NSW ministers Ian Macdonald and Eddie Obeid to face trial in 2019 |work=[[Guardian Australia]] |date=6 October 2017 |access-date=10 April 2018 |agency=[[Australian Associated Press|AAP]] }}</ref> All three were tried before Justice [[Elizabeth Fullerton]], and the trial commenced in early 2020 and concluded in February 2021. None of the accused gave evidence at their trial. Justice Fullerton handed down her verdict on 19 July, finding all three guilty.<ref name="SMHverdict2021">{{cite news|title=Eddie Obeid, Ian Macdonald and Moses Obeid found guilty over rigged tender |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/eddie-obeid-ian-macdonald-and-moses-obeid-found-guilty-over-rigged-tender-20210718-p58atd.html |access-date=19 July 2021 |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=19 July 2021 |author=McClymont, Kate |language=en-AU}}</ref><ref name="ABCverdict2021">{{cite news|title=Eddie Obied, Ian Macdonald, Moses Obeid found guilty of mine licence conspiracy |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-07-19/obeid-macdonald-found-guilty-of-mine-licence-conspiracy/100303688 |access-date=19 July 2021 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |date=19 July 2021 |author= |language=en-AU}}</ref><ref name="GAverdict2021">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jul/19/former-nsw-labor-ministers-eddie-obeid-and-ian-macdonald-found-guilty-of-corruption-charges |title=Former NSW Labor ministers Eddie Obeid and Ian Macdonald found guilty of corruption charges |author=Davies, Anne |work=[[Guardian Australia]] |date=19 July 2021 |access-date=19 July 2021 }}</ref> On 21 October, Macdonald was sentenced to nine years and six months, with a [[parole|non-parole]] period of five years and three months, over his part in the conspiracy to gain a mining lease over the Obeid's family farm at Bylong.<ref name="GAsentence2021">{{cite news |author=Davies, Anne |url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/oct/21/former-nsw-labor-powerbroker-eddie-obeid-sentenced-to-seven-years-in-jail |title=Ex-Labor powerbroker Eddie Obeid released on health grounds after being sentenced to seven years in jail |work=[[Guardian Australia]] |date=21 October 2021 |access-date=20 December 2021 }}</ref><ref name="SBSsentence2021">{{cite news |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/eddie-and-moses-obeid-ian-macdonald-jailed-over-conspiracy/7c0ccc50-e8a7-4826-858f-733585b26b99 |title=Eddie and Moses Obeid, Ian Macdonald jailed over conspiracy |work=[[SBS News]] |date=21 October 2021 |access-date=20 December 2021 |agency=[[Australian Associated Press|AAP]] }}</ref> Macdonald, together with Obeid, have lodged an appeal against their conviction, claiming that Justice Fullerton made a number of errors of fact and reasoning when she found them guilty. Despite applying for [[Bail#Australia|bail]], Macdonald is in custody with the appeal expected to be heard in September 2022,<ref>{{cite news |author=Wells, Janelle |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-12-17/eddie-obeid-moses-ian-macdonald-denied-bail-before-christmas/100708262 |title=Eddie Obeid, Moses Obeid and Ian Macdonald denied bail ahead of conspiracy appeal |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |location=Australia |date=17 December 2021 |access-date=20 December 2021 }}</ref> later delayed to April 2023.<ref name="abc-2022-06-23">{{Cite news |date=2022-06-23 |title=Jailed former NSW ministers to appeal convictions for $30m mine licence conspiracy |language=en-AU |work=ABC News |first=Jamelle|last=Wells|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-06-23/eddie-obeid-moses-obeid-ian-macdonald-appeal/101176340 |access-date=2022-10-21}}</ref>
